title: onprem-triage-daybook
content:
Midday quick log / triage - customer site (non-prod -> staging->prod rollout map)

Context:
- Customer: Meridian Payments (sandbox-to-prod pilot)
- Location: customer colo, eu-central region, private VPC (connected via VPN + dedicated transit)
- Purpose: validate onprem package, kernel/driver compatibility, and automated service recovery for inference pods
- Owner on site: IT lead Marco (works with our SRE partner)

Today timeline (10/11 - 10/12):
- 09:40 SSH into bastion (jump box) to confirm VPC peering and route table entries
  - quick check: sudo ip route | grep 10.0.
  - observed: route to 10.200.0.0/16 via eni-abc123 (ok)
- 10:10 Pulled installer v0.9.2 to /tmp, ran ./install.sh --profile=small-gpu --kms=enabled
  - output: failed at step "nv-driver-check" (exit 127) - missing kernel-headers for 5.15.x
  - note: customer kernel pinned to 5.15.2-rt. need matching kernel-headers repo (cust infra blocks standard repos)
- 10:45 Attempted local rebuild of kernel modules; modprobe nvidia returned "Unknown symbol in module"
- 11:20 Opened ticket with on-site infra to add internal package repo mirror (ACTION: Marco)

Blockers / current problems:
- Kernel headers mismatch: inability to compile nvidia module -> inference runtime cannot start on GPU nodes.
- Syslog shows repeated OOM kills for process redwood-serving (under memory pressure when batch>8). Suspect host cgroup config too tight.
- DISK pressure on /var/lib/docker (75% used) and ephemeral /scratch on GPU nodes has only 4GB free. Need cleanup or add tmpfs limits.
- SELinux is Enforcing; our systemd unit tries to access /mnt/local-cache, causing AVC denials in audit.log. Need policy tweaks or dedicated label.

Workarounds tried:
- Reduced batch_size to 1 in config.yaml -> runtime started but throughput unacceptable (used as stopgap for smoke tests)
- Started service with --no-kernel-modules to run CPU-only, validated model loading and end-to-end inference latency (p95 ~120ms for small model)
- Mounted additional EBS volume (temporary) to /var/lib/docker on one node; cleared old images -> freed 18GB

Important environment notes / reminders for final runbook:
- KMS: customer uses internal HSM with ARN arn:aws:kms:eu-central-1:111222333:key/xxxx (we only get wrapped keys) -> ensure installer requests key-grant beforehand; update installer to retry 2x on timeouts.
- Firewall: egress to s3 and our control-plane (api.redwood.ai) must be allowed on 443. Also open 1935/tcp for internal traffic between GPU nodes (used by TPU-adapter shim)
- IP ranges: customer uses 10.200.0.0/16 (private VPC) and 172.29.0.0/16 (k8s pod CIDR). Document these in terraform variables.
- Certs: internal CA cert expires 2025-03-01; advise renew in next maintenance window (customer aware).

Quick commands (notes to self)
- check driver: uname -r ; rpm -qa | grep kernel-headers ; ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/video
- journal tail: journalctl -u redwood-serving -n 200 --no-pager\- audit: ausearch -m avc -ts yesterday | tail -n 50
- docker cleanup: docker system prune -a --volumes (only after confirmation)

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Can infra team add internal package mirror and expose kernel-headers repo? (Marco to confirm ETA)
- Is it acceptable to ship a tiny shim that reduces memory footprint vs. asking customer to increase host cgroup memory? Need engineering decision.
- Confirm backup plan: if GPU nodes cannot be fixed within 48h, fallback to Dedicated staging pool and route traffic via temporary VPN endpoint; inform customer success and update runbook.

Next steps (priority order):
1) Push small installer patch: add retry logic for KMS handshake + clearer error message on kernel-header mismatch (PR 187 references). (Owner: Priya)
2) Coordinate with Marco to add package mirror + kernel-headers for 5.15.2-rt (Owner: Marco / Evan follow-up)
3) Draft SELinux policy change and test in staging; if not possible, add documented exception for /mnt/local-cache in systemd unit file. (Owner: Lina)
4) Schedule a short sync with CS (20m) to set expectations and possible Dedicated fallback (today afternoon). (Owner: Priya)
5) Clean up disk on two GPU nodes and verify docker image retention policy (Owner: on-site infra)

Notes for the final runbook (things to include):
- Preflight checklist (kernel version, kernel-headers, docker version, available disk, memory limits, selinux mode)
- Network requirements (egress to S3, control plane, internal ports + IP ranges)
- KMS/HSM handshake steps + required grants and IAM roles
- Fallback routing steps to Dedicated pool + VPN endpoint details
- Troubleshooting snippet: how to collect nv driver logs, capture /var/log/audit/audit.log, and aggregate journalctl for redwood-serving

Random side-jots (brain dump):
- If we proactively ship a tiny helper package to detect kernel/driver mismatch and provide exact install commands (mirror link + RPM names), it would cut field time by ~30-45m. Add to backlog.
- Consider adding a preflight systemd timer that runs checks and writes a single consolidated status.json to S3/consumer for support to pick up automatically.

End of midday log. Will update after 4pm sync with Marco and CS.

-- Priya
